title: Coverage — relatedness and what trees mean
summary: Coverage items: closest and most distant relatives, relatedness versus resemblance, the meaning of lines and nodes, and two-tier questions.

items.text: Tap the closest relative of the whale.
Tap the most distant relative of the whale.
Is the whale more closely related to the cow or to the frog?
Is the squirrel more closely related to the guinea pig or to the mouse?
Which tip is the whale's closest relative — and why?

reasons: The whale shares a more recent common ancestor with it than with any other tip.
The whale looks more like it than like any other tip.

items.text: On this tree, what does the point where two branches meet represent?

options: A common ancestor of the lineages that meet there
A point where two species look alike
A measurement of distance between tips

items.text: What does a branch — a line on this tree — represent?

options: How much DNA two tips share

items.text: Which tip on this tree is the most advanced?

options: No tip — every living lineage has been evolving for the same total time
The earthworm — it branched off first
The whale — it sits at the end of the longest chain of splits

items.text: The frog's lineage branched off before the other vertebrates here. Is the frog still evolving?

options: No — only lineages that split recently still evolve
No — it is a living fossil, unchanged since its ancestors
